subject: Lighthouse SIG: log TTL adjudication & evidence package request
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@lighthouse.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lighthouse Compliance <compliance@lighthouse.com>
Date: Sun, 6 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG/CAIQ follow-up — tenant-scoped log retention exception?

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the SIG follow-up earlier this week. One outstanding item from our security review: we need clarification and, if possible, an adjudication for a customer-specific deviation from your standard session/log retention policy.

Context: our product ingests ephemeral conversational traces and short-lived KV cache snapshots for correlation. Our regulatory team requires a 90-day window for a small subset of tenants under clinical trials; your standard ephemeral/session TTL appears to be 30 days. Please confirm:

- Whether Redwood supports an auditable, tenant-scoped retention carveout (i.e., extend TTL for only our trial-tenants).
- What evidence you can provide for deletion thereafter (proof-of-delete, export hashes, or deletion audit entries).
- Whether retaining longer introduces any SOC 2 or SIG implications we should flag internally.

I attached the SIG questionnaire excerpt and our proposed retention matrix for the affected tenants. Can you propose a timeline for an adjudication + evidence package? We’re aiming to complete our review by 12/22.

Appreciate the help — Elena

Attachments: sig-questionnaire-2026.pdf, log-retention-matrix.csv
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@lighthouse.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ follow-up — tenant-scoped log retention exception?

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the matrix. Short answer: yes, we can support a tenant-scoped retention extension for a bounded set of tenants, with accompanying evidence. Longer answer and proposed next steps below.

Proposed approach:
- Engineering will confirm what artifacts we can produce: deletion audit log entries, HMAC-anchored export manifests (proof-of-delete token), and a sample forensic export demonstrating the deletion pipeline.
- Legal/Compliance will draft a limited attestation for the carveout (scope, duration, compensating controls).
- We’ll produce a small evidence bundle for your SOC 2/SIG reviewer (CSV manifest + sample logs + attestation).

Timeline: I’ll ask engineering for a technical write-up by EOD tomorrow and a complete evidence package by 12/17. Can Marissa and Soojin confirm feasibility and what the attestation draft should include?

For clarity, we only plan to touch tenant-level TTLs (no global policy changes). I’ve CC’d Marissa (engineering lead, runtime) and Soojin (security/compliance) to own the technical and attestational pieces.

Best,
Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
Head of Field Security & Compliance (acting)
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Elena Morris <elena.morris@lighthouse.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ follow-up — tenant-scoped log retention exception?

Elena / Sean / Soojin — technical breakdown below (TL;DR at top).

TL;DR: We can implement tenant-scoped TTL extensions for the following artifacts: session transcripts (text generation traces), prefix/KV cache snapshots, and request/response metadata. Retention beyond our default 30d requires: a config flag at the tenant-routing layer + a short-term escrow copy (encrypted) while awaiting deletion to ensure reproducibility for audits. We can produce deletion audit entries, an HMAC-anchored export manifest, and a sample proof-of-delete token.

Details:
1) What we retain today
- Short-lived indices: conversational traces and request metadata are stored in tiered hot storage (30d default).
- KV cache snapshots: ephemeral snapshots persisted for cache warm-up; typical TTL 7d.
- Aggregated telemetry/metrics: anonymized and aggregated over 90d by default.

2) Tenant-scoped extension mechanism
- Implementation: a tenant config in the routing service toggles retention overrides. Overrides are scoped, rate-limited, and require an approved retention-profile id.
- Escrow: when TTL>30d, we create an encrypted escrow snapshot (AES-256) kept in a customer-scoped bucket labeled with the retention-profile id; it is automatically rotated and deleted per the profile.
- Audit trail: every TTL change triggers an immutable audit event (user, request-id, timestamp, rationale) written to our immutable event store (append-only) — visible in export.

3) Evidence we can produce
- Deletion audit CSV: entries covering the deletion job (timestamp, object-hash, tenant-id, retention-profile, operator-id).
- Proof-of-delete token: HMAC of deleted objects grouped per job + signed manifest (for your verifier).
- Sample forensic export: sanitized sample showing full lifecycle for one tenant (ingest -> storage -> deletion).

4) SIG/CAIQ considerations
- Control implications: extended TTL is an acceptable exception if documented and if compensating controls (encryption-at-rest, targeted access controls, monitoring) are applied. We will map to SIG sections (CCE-2, LOG-1, and retention-related CAIQ controls) in the attestation.

Open questions for Lighthouse:
- Exact tenant IDs you plan to include (we need canonical IDs to scope the override).
- Desired retention window (we can support 60/90/180 days but longer windows require legal approval).

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft attestation template (ttl-adjudication-draft-attestation.docx) and a sample CSV export layout (log-retention-matrix.csv).

If you can share the tenant IDs and confirm 90d, engineering will run a dry-run export and provide the sample artifacts by 12/15.

--
Marissa Cole
Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@lighthouse.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Lighthouse Compliance <compliance@lighthouse.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 08:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ follow-up — tenant-scoped log retention exception?

Elena — thanks Marissa, that level of detail is great. To be explicit about deliverables and timeline: 

Deliverables
- Technical evidence bundle: deletion audit CSV, HMAC manifest, sample sanitized export (by 12/15).
- Attestation doc: scope, compensating controls, duration, signed by Redwood security/compliance (draft by 12/13, final by 12/20).
- Implementation notes: tenant override configuration steps and rollback playbook.

Next steps for Lighthouse to unblock us:
1) Send canonical tenant IDs (format: tenant:PROJECT-xxxx).
2) Confirm desired retention window (you asked for 90d — confirm).
3) Confirm reviewers (name + email) who will receive the evidence package.

Sidenote: Marissa — engineering will run a simulated delete and store the job manifest in the internal HS-4821 Jira. I’ll attach the job output to the evidence bundle.

Elena — if that timeline works, we’ll proceed. If you need the attestation sooner, we can prioritize the draft earlier.

Best,
Sean
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@lighthouse.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lighthouse Compliance <compliance@lighthouse.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 17:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ follow-up — tenant-scoped log retention exception?

Sean / Marissa — thanks, that works. Quick answers:
- Tenant IDs: tenant:LIGHT-TRIAL-021, tenant:LIGHT-TRIAL-022
- Retention window: confirm 90 days for both tenants.
- Reviewers: Elena Morris (me) and Karen Osei <karen.osei@lighthouse.com> (security reviewer)

Please prioritize the draft attestation and the deletion manifest sample. We’ll expect the evidence bundle by 12/15 and will flag any SIG follow-ups quickly.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

— Elena
